subject: The Dance We Do
comment: Hi All, Last night was interesting. I sat behind the new Chief's family and was embarrassed. What I saw made me very uncomfortable and I could not help but believe what I felt was caused by seeing more of the same old, all over again. What I heard was people and institutions, both taking credit for all the good they did, and at the same time blaming each other because we did not do enough good or help enough people to change the conversation. More of the same old... all over again. The same old dance. I talked with several City employees before the meeting and some knew and some were unbelieving when the discussion focused on what was not helping the homeless in our community. The folks who wanted to believe programs were working, could not believe it when SLCPD officers said that they were arresting the same folks over and over again ... and they struggled when the officers said the homeless folks being arrested had been in a number of programs and were still sleeping on the street. I'll be talking with a local high school today, not only about our program but about what they can really do "to help" the mentally ill and addicted living on our streets. And that is to ask better questions. I will ask them to not believe their professors, elected officials or pastors when they tell them how to do this or that or what is effective or is not effective. Because what the letters "think works" and teach has created what we have today. I will ask them to ask their professors and anyone who claims something "works" for the data they don't have. I want to encourage them to doubt and become part of the solution that brings real change to a system that seems unwilling to acknowledge its shortcomings. The Parking Group said they follow your lead. You tell them what to do. I am suggesting that The City Council take the lead when funding any city department working with the homeless. Start asking funded programs to gather information on how effective a program is before and after they are funded. Help SLCPD and the youth in our community by making sure what we say is working is working. The officers are frustrated. I know, I talked with them not only before and them after the meeting last night but have talked with them for years. I am working with high school and college students and I am asking them to doubt, not only what they believe, but what the "experts" tell them. And they are starting to listen. The City Council can play a major role, no not major, but be the force that makes the change we need happen just by walking the talk and holding programs and departments that are funded accountable by ensuring they do "walk the talk". And just something I need to say. I did not know the person who called in and asked for support for our program. And Polly asked her Mom if she could do what she did last night. No one encouraged her... she was just being herself. We all can do better, nope... we have to do better. Let's find some new music to dance to, Bernie

subject: It's Tuesday
comment: Hi All, Two things. One: I understand the Legislature passed SB 0078. The bill creates a much-needed Ombudsman for the homeless. The homeless desperately need an independent voice advocating for them in a system that routinely puts its own needs before the needs of those it serves. History does not speak well for what will happen. The Legislature recently commissioned two audits, one focused on homeless services and the other on our court system. The audits found neither the courts or homeless services were meeting the needs of the homeless. The audits were great. The problem is no one has read them, and the problems they pointed out are still major problems. HB 298 was passed last year and it intended to address the same problems, but since being passed, it has been collecting dust in someone's closet. And now we have the new position of Ombudsman. Will whoever is appointed read the audits and address the fact that no one is being held accountable for anything? Our jails are full, the number of homeless is increasing, and everyone is still getting more and more funding and nothing is changing. Or will the Ombudsman's desk be put in the same closet as those audits and copies of HB 298? Two: We have moved back to the library... with a twist. We are now on both sides of 200E and we will start reaching out to a really troubling segment of the homeless population. Those audited mental health and addiction services and courts are the same institutions school kids are in when they first get into trouble. When Foster Care and Special Ed programs fail to meet their needs, many end up in trouble and eventually in jail and on the street. A number of these no longer young folks are in our program. We will reach out to any adult on the street who first entered the system while still in school and ask them to join us. We will start documenting their experiences. When city staffers look out the window in the morning... I hope they wonder how young some of the people they see were when they first entered the publicly funded "we can help you" system. The folks they see once lived in a home and were cared about... and they asked for help... they needed help... and ... just look out the window and you will not have to read the audits to know how well the current "we can help you" system works. Bernie
